subject.declared_domain: The governed anchor vocabulary for the C3 overlapping-domain-cover: which constituent node types DEFINE a C3 domain (ANCHOR_CATALOG) and which are excluded from ever anchoring one (HUB_TYPES). Two module-level literals read at runtime by the C3 cover and by the CVO composition harness.

methodology.how: Two hand-authored Python literals, not derived from anything. ANCHOR_CATALOG maps 5 domain names to sets of node types; HUB_TYPES is a flat set of 3. Membership in the cover is 'a motif CONTAINS a catalog anchor', so these literals ARE the definition of what a C3 system can be about. THE BURIED OPINIONS, IN PROSE because the TO's form is prose, and on this subject the opinions are the entire content: (1) FIVE DOMAINS, hand-picked -- object-data, compute-orchestration, pipeline, table-data, identity -- not a derived partition of anything, so a resource class outside these five cannot anchor a system at all; (2) HUB-EXCLUSION IS IMPLEMENTED BY ABSENCE -- LAMBDA, EC2_INSTANCE and 'actor' are excluded by NOT BEING LISTED, with an assert as the only guard, so a future editor adding a hub type to the catalog gets an AssertionError rather than a design conversation; (3) TWO OF THE EIGHT ANCHOR TYPES ARE NOT AWS-SHAPED -- PipelineScript and PipelineFunction are repo/pipeline-space, so the catalog silently spans two identity spaces; (4) the stated rationale for hub exclusion is that hubs 'create overlap, never define a domain', which is a modelling judgement recorded in a comment and nowhere a consumer can branch on.
declared_opinions: FIVE HAND-PICKED DOMAINS (object-data, compute-orchestration, pipeline, table-data, identity) -- not a derived partition of anything, so a resource class outside these five cannot anchor a C3 system at all.

HUB-EXCLUSION IS IMPLEMENTED BY ABSENCE: LAMBDA, EC2_INSTANCE and 'actor' are excluded by NOT BEING LISTED, with an assert as the only guard, so the exclusion is invisible to anyone reading the catalog alone.

TWO OF THE EIGHT ANCHOR TYPES ARE NOT AWS-SHAPED -- PipelineScript and PipelineFunction are repo/pipeline space -- so the catalog silently spans at least two identity spaces in one equality-matched set.
The stated rationale for hub exclusion is that hubs 'create overlap, never define a domain' -- a modelling judgement recorded in a source comment and nowhere a consumer can branch on.
The >=2-member promotion threshold (in the cover that consumes this catalog) decides when a domain becomes a C3System; single-member domains stay C2. An arbitrary cut with no recorded derivation.

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: EXERCISED: a motif whose constituent types match NO catalog anchor is returned in the cover's 'orphans' list -- a named coverage flag, not a silent drop. A domain with exactly 1 member motif is returned in 'unpromoted' rather than discarded. An anchor set overlapping HUB_TYPES raises AssertionError at cover time.
silent_degrade_paths: ⛔ A NODE TYPE THAT DISAPPEARS FROM THE ESTATE LEAVES NO TRACE HERE. If S3Key stopped being emitted, the catalog would still list it, the cover would find no motifs containing it, and the affected domain would simply produce fewer systems -- indistinguishable from a domain that is genuinely small. Nothing compares the catalog against the graph's live type vocabulary in either direction.

⛔ THE ORPHANS LIST CONFLATES TWO CAUSES, MEASURED BY EXERCISE: a motif carrying a genuinely NEW node type and a motif that is genuinely un-anchored BOTH land in orphans, with nothing distinguishing them. So the flag is honest that something was uncovered, and silent about WHY.
The assert guarding hub-exclusion fires only if someone adds a hub type TO the catalog; REMOVING a type from HUB_TYPES silently permits it to anchor a domain, with no guard at all.

LATENT, NOT LIVE, and scoped deliberately: ab_c3_cover:335 does m.split(':',1)[1] on every member nid with no guard, so a motif nid without a colon raises IndexError. Every live nid carries a 'c2:' prefix, so this is not a live defect -- I surfaced it only because my FIRST exercise fixture used colon-free nids and crashed. The fixture was unrealistic, not the code, and I corrected the fixture rather than reporting a defect that does not exist in the live population.

verdict.why: Every row worked, defects named with owners, usable within stated limits -- and this is the one subject in the TO whose CONTENT IS ENTIRELY OPINION, which makes it the most important card here for the canonical-materializer consumer. WHAT HOLDS: it is a genuine source (authored, not derived, and editing it changes the world); the cover's orphan and unpromoted lists are honest coverage flags rather than silent drops; hub exclusion carries a written rationale. WHAT QUALIFIES IT: (1) the catalog SPANS AT LEAST TWO IDENTITY SPACES in one flat equality-matched set -- 6 AWS types, 2 pipeline-space types, and 'actor' again elsewhere -- with NO declared mapping and no need for one, because string equality hides the question; (2) FIVE HAND-PICKED DOMAINS decide what a C3 system can be about, and nothing compares them against the estate's live node-type vocabulary in either direction; (3) hub exclusion is implemented by ABSENCE with an assert as its only guard; (4) the governed vocabulary for the C3 layer lives in one seat's deliverables folder rather than a standards location. ⛔ AND A CORRECTION THIS CARD CARRIES: my own wave-1 TO stated 'SEVEN hand-listed AWS node types'; it is EIGHT, and two of them are not AWS. || SEMANTIC-AXIS DECLARATION: on this subject the semantic axis is the ONLY axis, and I examined it PARTIALLY, not systematically. I enumerated four opinions from the source, but I did NOT establish whether the 5 domains were ever derived from anything, whether >=2 is a considered threshold or a round number, or whether the vocabulary matches the graph today. ⛔ No instrument I hold reaches that: an AST parse tells me what the literal SAYS, never whether it is still RIGHT. || GENERATOR CURRENCY: materializer_standing='canonical', basis INFERRED -- it is the catalog the live cover reads and I found no competitor, but I did not establish that none exists.
